cetiosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Cetiosaurus (The question of the type species)

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived between 171 and 165 million years ago in what is now Britain and possibly France.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus ( meaning 'whale lizard', from the Greek /κήτειος meaning 'sea monster' (later, 'whale') and /σαυρος meaning 'lizard'), is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Period, living about 171 to 165 million years ago during the Bajocian and Bathonian ages in what is now Britain and probably France.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was the first sauropod dinosaur to be described from bones, named in 1842 by Sir Richard Owen.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus was named in 1842, making it the first sauropod from which bones were described and is the most complete sauropod found in England.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck, small head, relatively long forelimbs, and a shorter tail compared to most sauropods.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus was a quadrupedal, long-necked, small-headed herbivore. It had a shorter tail and neck than most sauropods. The forelimbs on the other hand, were relatively long.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of about 16 meters and a weight of roughly 11 tons.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have been about 16 m long and to have weighed roughly 11 t.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen named the genus Cetiosaurus in 1841, one year before he coined the term Dinosauria.
facts.quote: In 1841 biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist Sir Richard Owen, named these as the genus Cetiosaurus, the year before he coined the term Dinosauria.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen initially classified Cetiosaurus as a gigantic sea-dwelling reptile rather than a dinosaur, a view reflected in the genus name meaning 'sea-monster'.
facts.quote: Owen initially did not recognise Cetiosaurus for a dinosaur but considered it a gigantic sea-dwelling reptile. This was reflected by the name, derived from Greek κήτειος, kèteios, "sea-monster".

facts.statement: In 1868 and 1869, workers and Professor John Phillips discovered three skeletons and additional bone material of a sauropod near Bletchingdon in a Bathonian layer.
facts.quote: In March 1868, workers near Bletchingdon discovered a sauropod right femur. Between March 1869 and June 1870 Professor John Phillips, further investigating the site, in a layer dating from the Bathonian uncovered three skeletons and additional bone material.

facts.statement: In 1871, Professor John Phillips named two species based on the Bletchingdon finds: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis and Cetiosaurus glymptonensis.
facts.quote: In 1871 based on these he named two species: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis (originally spelled Ceteosaurus Oxoniensis) and Cetiosaurus glymptonensis.

facts.statement: A new specimen of C. oxoniensis, known as the 'Rutland Dinosaur', was unknowingly excavated on June 19, 1968, from discarded ironstone near Great Casterton, Rutland.
facts.quote: A century later, a new C. oxoniensis specimen (LCM G468.1968), subsequently named by the local media, the "Rutland Dinosaur", was unknowingly excavated on 19 June 1968 in the form of several tons of discarded siderite ironstone from a clay-pit near Great Casterton, Rutland

facts.statement: A provisional identification of the Rutland Dinosaur specimen as C. oxoniensis was published in late 1970 by curator Michael Jones after examination and corroboration by Professor J. S. McIntosh.
facts.quote: It was not until late 1970 however that a provisional identification of C. oxoniensis was published by curator Michael Jones following examination and corroboration by Prof. J S McIntosh of the Peabody Museum of Natural History Yale University

facts.statement: The C. oxoniensis specimen displayed at Leicester Museum and Art Gallery is 15 meters long and consists of fourteen cervical, ten dorsal, five sacral, and about fifty caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specimen on display at Leicester Museum and Art Gallery is 15 m (49 ft) in length and has fourteen cervical vertebrae, ten dorsals, five sacrals and about fifty caudals.

facts.statement: C. oxoniensis was officially designated as the type species of the genus Cetiosaurus in 2014.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis was officially made the new type species in 2014.

facts.statement: Fossils once assigned to Cetiosaurus have been found mainly in England, but also in France, Switzerland, and Morocco.
facts.quote: Fossilized remains once assigned to Cetiosaurus have mainly been found in England but also in France, Switzerland and Morocco.

facts.statement: It was determined in 1849 that some bones previously assigned to Cetiosaurus actually belonged to Iguanodontidae rather than sauropods.
facts.quote: As became apparent in 1849, some of these bones were not sauropod in nature at all but of Iguanodontidae.

facts.statement: A 2003 study could not locate two tail vertebrae attributed to the Blisworth skeleton in the Natural History Museum's collections.
facts.quote: However in a 2003 paper on the taxonomy of Cetiosaurus, neither of the two vertebrae were able to be located in the museum's collections by the paper's authors.

facts.statement: John Whitaker Hulke named Cetiosaurus humerocristatus in 1874 based on a humerus found at Sandsfoot near Weymouth in Dorset.
facts.quote: In 1874, John Whitaker Hulke named Cetiosaurus humerocristatus, "with a crested humerus", based on specimen BMNH 44635, a humerus found that year at Sandsfoot near Weymouth in Dorset.

facts.statement: In 2010, the species Cetiosaurus humerocristatus was reclassified into the separate genus Duriatitan.
facts.quote: In 2010, this was made a separate genus Duriatitan.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis leedsii was named in 1887 by John Hulke based on fossils collected by Alfred Nicholson Leeds from the Oxford Clay.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis leedsii was named in 1887 by John Hulke for a pelvis, vertebrae and ribs collected by Alfred Nicholson Leeds, an English farmer and amateur fossil collector who throughout his life compiled numerous collections of fossils from the Oxford Clay.

facts.statement: Arthur Smith Woodward placed Cetiosaurus leedsi in the genus Cetiosaurus in 1905, including a partial skeleton from Peterborough, England.
facts.quote: Arthur Smith Woodward supported Seeley's classification scheme in 1905, placing C. leedsi in Cetiosaurus, including within C. leedsi a partial sauropod skeleton collected from the Oxford Clay of Peterborough, England.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene assigned Cetiosaurus leedsi to the separate genus Cetiosauriscus in 1927.
facts.quote: In 1927, Friedrich von Huene assigned C. leedsi to the separate genus Cetiosauriscus.

facts.statement: Rodney Steel renamed the species Cardiodon to Cetiosaurus rugulosus in 1970 based on a lost tooth.
facts.quote: In 1970 Rodney Steel renamed Cardiodon Owen 1841, based on a now lost tooth, into Cetiosaurus rugulosus, "the wrinkled one".

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin rejected the identity of Cetiosaurus rugulosus in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, Upchurch & Martin rejected the identity.

facts.statement: Henri Émile Sauvage named Cetiosaurus rigauxi in 1874 based on a vertebra found at Le Portel in layers dating from the Tithonian.
facts.quote: In 1874, Henri Émile Sauvage named Cetiosaurus rigauxi based on a vertebra found by Edouard Edmond Joseph Rigaux at Le Portel, west of Boulogne-sur-Mer, in layers dating from the Tithonian.

facts.statement: In 1903, Sauvage concluded that Cetiosaurus rigauxi represented a pliosaurid.
facts.quote: In 1903, however, he was forced to conclude it represented a pliosaurid.

facts.statement: Henri Émile Sauvage named the species Cetiosaurus philippsi in 1880.
facts.quote: In 1880, Sauvage named another species: Cetiosaurus philippsi.

facts.statement: The specific name mogrebiensis refers to the Maghreb region.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Maghreb.

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch and John Martin determined in 2003 that Cetiosaurus hypoolithicus and Cetiosaurus epioolithicus were invalid because they were nomina nuda.
facts.quote: In 2003, Paul Upchurch and John Martin determined that C. "hypoolithicus" and C. "epioolithicus" could not be used because they were nomina nuda.

facts.statement: Of four species named by Owen in 1842, only Cetiosaurus brevis was not considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Of the four species named in Owen's second 1842 article, C. brevis, C. brachyurus, C. longus and C. medius, only C. brevis would not be a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin changed their position in 2009 regarding the type species of Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: However, in 2009, when their request was officially filed, Upchurch and Martin had changed their position.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin still advocated changing the type species because Cetiosaurus medius was known only from undiagnostic material.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, they still advocated a change in type because C. medius is known only from undiagnostic material.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, named by Phillips in 1871, is the type species of the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: The complex naming history can be summarised in a list of Cetiosaurus species: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis Phillips, 1871: type species of Cetiosaurus

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus brachyurus, named by Owen in 1842, is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus brachyurus Owen, 1842: nomen dubium

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus longus, named by Owen in 1842, is a nomen dubium now assigned to Cetiosauriscus longus.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus longus Owen, 1842: nomen dubium; = Cetiosauriscus longus (Owen, 1842) McIntosh, 1990

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus medius, named by Owen in 1842, is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus medius Owen, 1842: nomen dubium

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus giganteus, cited by Huxley in 1870, is a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus giganteus Owen vide Huxley, 1870: nomen nudum

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus rigauxi, named by Sauvage in 1874, is not a sauropod but a pliosaurid.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus rigauxi Sauvage, 1874: non Cetiosaurus, pliosaurid

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus leedsi, named by Hulke in 1887, is a nomen dubium originally described as Ornithopsis leedsii.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus leedsi (Hulke, 1887) Woodward, 1905: nomen dubium; = Ornithopsis leedsii Hulke, 1887

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus rugulosus, renamed by Steel in 1970, is not in the genus Cetiosaurus but is classified as Cardiodon.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus rugulosus (Owen, 1845) Steel, 1970: non Cetiosaurus, = Cardiodon Owen, 1841; = Cardiodon rugulosus Owen, 1845

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis, named by de Lapparent in 1955, is not considered to belong to the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis de Lapparent, 1955: non Cetiosaurus

facts.statement: Fossil tracks discovered in Oxfordshire in 1997 and 2024 are suggested to be Cetiosaurus footprints, though they could also belong to a diplodocoid.
facts.quote: Several fossil tracks discovered in 1997 and 2024 at two Oxfordshire, UK sites have been suggested to be Cetiosaurus footprints, though identification with a diplodocoid is also possible.

facts.statement: Vertebrae of a related species were found in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis hulkei (which had been described by Harry Seeley in 1870 based on vertebrae from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight in southern England),

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus rigauxi fossils were found in layers dating from the Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: In 1874, Henri Émile Sauvage named Cetiosaurus rigauxi based on a vertebra found by Edouard Edmond Joseph Rigaux at Le Portel, west of Boulogne-sur-Mer, in layers dating from the Tithonian.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis fossils were found in the El Mers Formation dating to the Bathonian stage.
facts.quote: In 1955, Albert-Félix de Lapparent named Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis based on three skeletons found in Morocco from the El Mers Formation dating to the Bathonian.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis is the best-known species from the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis, the best known species from the Middle Jurassic, which the genus Cetiosaurus had generally come to be identified with.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cetiosaurus humerocristatus is a valid taxon, as it is often considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: This today is often considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cetiosaurus mogrebiensis is a valid taxon, though it is often seen as not belonging to the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: This is today sometimes seen as a valid taxon, but one not belonging to Cetiosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cetiosaurus brevis should be the type species, as this would cause taxonomic instability with the genus Pelorosaurus.
facts.quote: This conclusion, if correct, would cause considerable taxonomic instability, because the genus Pelorosaurus had since been based on its fossils, and recognized as a totally different kind of sauropod.

facts.statement: The genus Cetiosaurus is known from three skeletons discovered by the Phillips family.
facts.quote: These include the three skeletons found by Phillips.

facts.statement: A larger skeleton catalogued with multiple numbers was selected by Upchurch and Martin as the lectotype for the species C. oxoniensis.
facts.quote: One of these is a larger animal (catalogued as OUMNH J13605–13613, J13615–16, J13619–J13688 and J13899), which was chosen by Upchurch & Martin as the lectotype of the species

facts.statement: A roughly 40% complete skeleton from Rutland significantly increased the known skeletal elements, particularly in the neck region.
facts.quote: The Rutland specimen, about 40% complete, increases considerably the number of known skeletal elements, especially in the neck.

facts.statement: The skull of Cetiosaurus is largely unknown, though a brain case may be represented by specimen OUMNH J13596.
facts.quote: The skull is largely unknown, perhaps with the exception of the brain case represented by specimen OUMNH J13596.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Cetiosaurus at 16 meters and its mass at 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length at 16 m and body mass at 11 t.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus had forelimbs equal in length to its hindlimbs because its forearm was as long as its upper arm, unlike most other sauropods.
facts.quote: Its forearm was as long as the upper arm, unlike most other sauropods, resulting in a forelimb equalling the hindlimb in length.

facts.statement: The thigh bone of Cetiosaurus was approximately six feet long.
facts.quote: Its thigh bone was approximately six feet long.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin identified five unique derived traits (autapomorphies) for C. oxoniensis in their 2003 revision of the genus.
facts.quote: In their 2003 revision of the genus, Upchurch & Martin identified five autapomorphies of C. oxoniensis.

facts.statement: The rear neck and front back vertebrae of Cetiosaurus have low, symmetrical, pyramid-shaped spines on their tops.
facts.quote: The rear neck vertebrae and the front back vertebrae have spines on their tops that are low, symmetrical and in the shape of a pyramid.

facts.statement: The lower process of the ilium features a triangular depression on the outer surface of its base where the pubic bone was attached.
facts.quote: The lower process of the ilium, to which the pubic bone was attached, features on the outer surface of its base a triangular depression.

facts.statement: Thomas Huxley explicitly stated in 1869 that Cetiosaurus was a dinosaur.
facts.quote: In 1869 Thomas Huxley stated explicitly that Cetiosaurus was a dinosaur.

facts.statement: Lydekker assigned Cetiosaurus to its own family, the Cetiosauridae, in 1888.
facts.quote: In 1888 Lydekker assigned Cetiosaurus to its own family: the Cetiosauridae.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic research has not produced a single clear consensus on the position of Cetiosaurus oxoniensis within the sauropod family tree.
facts.quote: Modern exact cladistic research has not resulted in a single clear outcome about the position of Cetiosaurus oxoniensis in the sauropod tree.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Medio

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was the first sauropod whose bones were described in 1842.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue en 1842 el primer saurópodo del que se describieron los huesos

facts.statement: The species C. oxoniensis is based on three more or less complete specimens discovered starting from 1868.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis se basa en tres especímenes más o menos completos, descubiertos a partir de 1868 en adelante.

facts.statement: The genus Cetiosaurus was named by Owen in 1841.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Owen, 1841

facts.statement: The type species Cetiosaurus oxoniensis was named by Phillips in 1871.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Phillips, 1871

facts.statement: C. oxoniensis was a primitive herbivore, quadrupedal, with a long neck and small head.
facts.quote: C. oxoniensis era un herbívoro "primitivo", cuadrúpedo , de cuello largo y cabeza pequeña .

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus had a shorter tail and neck than most sauropods.
facts.quote: Tenía cola y cuello más cortos que la mayoría de los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus had relatively long forelimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores, por otro lado, eran relativamente largas.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus lived in an environment of floodplains and open woodlands.
facts.quote: The environment in which Cetiosaurus lived was floodplain and open woodland.

facts.statement: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist that ate at both low and medium-high levels, based on its moderately long neck and limb proportions.
facts.quote: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist, eating at both a low and a medium-high level, in view of its moderately long neck and limb proportions.

facts.statement: It is debated why the dinosaurs of the London-Brabant Massif did not experience insular dwarfism despite the island's size.
facts.quote: It has been questioned why the dinosaurs of the island did not experience insular dwarfism, as would be expected for an island of this size.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was named because its describer, Sir Richard Owen, initially thought it was a marine creature like a huge crocodile and did not recognize it as a land dinosaur.
facts.quote: Fue llamado así porque su descriptor, Sir Richard Owen que supuso que se trataba de una criatura marina , inicialmente un cocodrilo extremadamente grande y no lo reconoció como un dinosaurio terrestre.

facts.statement: Due to the early description, eighteen species were eventually named in the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Debido a la descripción temprana, muchas especies serían nombradas en el género, finalmente dieciocho de ellas.

facts.statement: The species Cetiosaurus brachyurus, Cetiosaurus medius, and Cetiosaurus philippsi are listed as subdivisions of the genus.
facts.quote: subdivision: Cetiosaurus brachyurus? Owen, 1842 Cetiosaurus medius? Owen, 1842 Cetiosaurus philippsi? Sauvage, 1880

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was a primitive long-necked quadrupedal herbivore that reached 18 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue un primitivo herbívoro cuadrúpedo de cuello largo que alcanzó los 18 metros de largo

facts.statement: Its neck was as long as its body, and its tail was considerably longer, consisting of at least 40 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Su cuello era del mismo largo que su cuerpo, y la cola era considerablemente más larga, consistiendo en por lo menos 40 vértebras caudales

facts.statement: Its dorsal vertebrae were heavy and primitive, unlike the hollow bones of advanced sauropods like Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras dorsales, los huesos a lo largo de la espalda, eran pesadas y primitivas, diferentes de los huesos ahuecados de los saurópodos avanzados como Brachiosaurus

facts.statement: Its ulna was nearly as long as the humerus, unlike most other sauropods.
facts.quote: Su ulna, era casi tan larga como el húmero, a diferencia de la mayoría de los otros saurópodos

facts.statement: Its femur was approximately 1.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Su fémur era aproximadamente 1,2 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist that ate at low to medium-high levels based on its moderately long neck and limb proportions.
facts.quote: Paul consideró Cetiosaurus un generalista de alimentación, comiendo a un nivel bajo y medio alto, en vista de sus proporciones moderadamente largas de cuello y extremidades

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length at 16 meters and the weight at 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó la longitud del cuerpo a 16 metros, el peso en 11 toneladas

facts.statement: With the spines of all dorsal vertebrae, a crest is absent between the neural spine and the diapophysis.
facts.quote: Con las espinas de todas las vértebras dorsales, una cresta está ausente entre la espina dorsal y la diapófisis

facts.statement: The middle tail vertebrae have a tongue-shaped process on the top of the anterior face of the vertebral body.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola del medio tienen un proceso en forma de lengua en la parte superior de la cara frontal del cuerpo vertebral

facts.statement: The inferior process of the ilium, to which the pubis was attached, presents a triangular depression on the external surface of its base.
facts.quote: El proceso inferior del ilion, al que se unió el hueso púbico, presenta en la superficie externa de su base una depresión triangular

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was the first sauropod discovered.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue el primer saurópodo descubierto

facts.statement: In the 1830s, before it was named, expert George Cuvier identified those fossils as whale bones.
facts.quote: En la década de 1830s, antes de que se nombrara, el experto George Cuvier identificó esos fósiles como huesos de ballena

facts.statement: In 1841, after discovering two more specimens, Richard Owen suggested naming this specimen Cetiosaurus because it resembled a "whale-reptil" in some sense.
facts.quote: En 1841, tras haber descubierto 2 ejemplares más, Richard Owen sugirió llamar a este espécimen Cetiosaurus, ya que en cierto sentido se asemejaba mucho a un "reptil ballena"

facts.statement: Its true nature was not observed until Thomas Huxley named it a dinosaur in 1869.
facts.quote: La naturaleza verdadera no fue observada hasta que Thomas Huxley lo nombrara como un dinosaurio en 1869

facts.statement: In 1979, a Cetiosaurus femur was found in Morocco that was almost as tall as a soccer goal.
facts.quote: En 1979 se encontró el fémur de un cetiosaurio en Marruecos que era casi tan alto como una portería de fútbol

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus was, with the exception of the tooth genus Cardiodon, the first sauropod to be discovered and named, as well as the most known sauropod of England.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus fue, con la excepción del género de los dientes Cardiodon, el primer saurópodo en ser descubierto y nombrado así como el saurópodo más conocido de Inglaterra

facts.statement: The first fossils, vertebrae, and limb elements, were discovered near Chipping Norton at the beginning of the century and reported by collector John Kingdon in a letter read on June 3, 1825, to the Geological Society.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles, vértebras y elementos de las extremidades, fueron descubiertos cerca de Chipping Norton a principios del y fueron informados por el coleccionista John Kingdon en una carta leída el 3 de junio de 1825 a la Sociedad Geológica

facts.statement: It shared territory with predators like Megalosaurus and Eustreptospondylus in an environment of floodplains and open woodlands.
facts.quote: Compartió el territorio con predadores con el Megalosaurus y Eustreptospondylus en un ambiente de llanura inundable y bosques abiertos

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis lived in the Middle Jurassic of Oxfordshire and Rutland.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, del Jurásico Medio de Oxfordshire y Rutland

facts.statement: Fossil remains once assigned to Cetiosaurus have been found mainly in England but also in France, Switzerland, and Morocco.
facts.quote: Los restos fosilizados una vez asignados a Cetiosaurus se han encontrado principalmente en Inglaterra pero también en Francia, Suiza y Marruecos

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, from the Middle Jurassic of Oxfordshire and Rutland, is better known than the type species C. brevis and was proposed by Upchurch to be considered a neotype.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis, del Jurásico Medio de Oxfordshire y Rutland, es mejor conocido que la especie tipo C. brevis y fue propuesto por Upchurch para que sea considerado un neotipo

facts.statement: The material of C. medius is insufficient to include it in Cetiosaurus, so it is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: El material de C. medius es insuficiente para incluirlo en Cetiosaurus por lo que se lo considera nomen dubium

facts.statement: Numerous species have been assigned to Cetiosaurus over the years belonging to several different groups of sauropod dinosaurs. Therefore, the genus functioned as a typical "wastebasket taxon".
facts.quote: Numerosas especies han sido asignadas a Cetiosaurus a través delos años pertenecientes a varios grupos diferentes de dinosaurios saurópodos. Por lo tanto, el género funcionaba como un típico "taxón cajón de sastre"

facts.statement: As became evident in 1849, some of these bones were not sauropods but belonged to Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: Como se hizo evidente en 1849, algunos de estos huesos no eran saurópodos sino de Iguanodontidae

facts.statement: Owen thought it had crocodilian characteristics.
facts.quote: Owen pensó que tenía características de crocodilia

facts.statement: Owen initially did not recognize Cetiosaurus as a dinosaur but considered it a gigantic reptile that lived in the sea.
facts.quote: Owen inicialmente no reconoció a Cetiosaurus como un dinosaurio, pero lo consideró un gigantesco reptil que habitaba en el mar

facts.statement: Workers near Bletchingdon discovered the right femur of a sauropod in March 1868.
facts.quote: En marzo de 1868, los trabajadores cerca de Bletchingdon descubrieron el fémur derecho de un saurópodo.

facts.statement: This specimen is the most complete sauropod fossil and one of the most complete dinosaur specimens ever found in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Es el fósil de saurópodo más completo y uno de los especímenes más completos de un dinosaurio jamás encontrado en el Reino Unido.

facts.statement: Interest in the fossil did not arise until around 1980.
facts.quote: Fue solo alrededor de 1980 que hubo interés en el fósil.

facts.statement: It took approximately four years to locate the dinosaur bones.
facts.quote: Tomó alrededor de cuatro años encontrar los huesos de los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: The incomplete fossil is 15 meters long and has been exhibited since 1985 at the New Walk Museum in Leicester.
facts.quote: El fósil incompleto tiene 15 metros de largo y se ha exhibido desde 1985 en el Museo New Walk en Leicester.

facts.statement: Much of what is displayed to the public is a replica rather than the actual dinosaur.
facts.quote: Mucho de lo que se puede ver en la pantalla es una réplica, y no el dinosaurio real.

facts.statement: The model's spine consists of fourteen cervical, ten dorsal, five sacral, and approximately fifty caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral del modelo que se ve en la pantalla tiene catorce cervicales, diez dorsales, cinco sacras y alrededor de cincuenta caudales.

facts.statement: In 2010, Cetiosaurus humerocristatus was reclassified as a separate genus, Duriatitan.
facts.quote: En 2010, este se hizo un género separado Duriatitan.

facts.statement: C. leedsi is still considered a nomen dubium today.
facts.quote: Este aun hoy endía se considera un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Upchurch and Martin rejected this identification in 2003.
facts.quote: En 2003, Upchurch y Martin rechazaron la identidad.

facts.statement: In 1903, Sauvage concluded that the specimen represented a plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1903, se vio obligado a concluir que representaba un pliosáurido.

facts.statement: Sauvage named another species, C. philippsi, in 1880.
facts.quote: En 1880, Sauvage nombró a otra especie, C. philippsi.

facts.statement: Albert-Félix de Lapparent named C. mogrebiensis in 1955 based on three skeletons found in the El Mers formation in Morocco dating to the Bathonian.
facts.quote: En 1955, Albert-Félix de Lapparent llamó C. mogrebiensis basado en tres esqueletos encontrados en Marruecos en la formación El Mers que data de Batoniano.

facts.statement: Today, this taxon is considered valid but does not belong to the genus Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Hoy en día se lo ve como un taxón válido, pero uno que no pertenece a Cetiosaurus.

facts.statement: C. greppini is now considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Hoy se considera un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus belongs to the parent group Gravisauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gravisauria
